Superyacht Concept Project White Arrow Is Designed To Be a Luxurious Floating Sanctuary
6 photos
Photo: Nuvolari Lenard
As modern superyacht owners are looking for vessels that can serve as more than just luxurious holiday escapes, designers are finding ways to create concepts envisioned from the get-go as private floating residences, designed to make life on the water more comfortable, personal, and enjoyable.
Nuvolari Lenard, one of the most active and renowned yacht design firms in the world, has unveiled a new superyacht concept aimed specifically at this new generation of owners. It’s called Project White Arrow and blurs the line between a watercraft for maritime exploration and a luxury floating home.
A 116-meter (380-foot) behemoth, this new yacht concept is designed for seafarers who want to live full-time at sea, with generous living quarters, modern wellness facilities, and a setting meant to facilitate a deeper connection with the surrounding ocean.
Developed in collaboration with Florida-based brokerage and yacht management firm Moran Yacht & Ship, White Arrow builds on Nuvolari’s heritage while also taking into consideration current trends and the desires of future owners.
The vessel is presented as a ready-to-build project, but instead of offering a finished, fixed design, it’s more of a starting point, allowing future owners to tailor its architecture, interior design, and onboard features to their tastes and needs, with a focus on the quality of the onboard experience .
Photo: Nuvolari Lenard “Project White Arrow reflects this changing ‘sentiment’, exploring how scale, architecture and design can create an environment that feels both exceptional and deeply liveable,” declared studio co-founder Carlo Nuvolari. “A yacht of this scale gives you an extraordinary opportunity, but also a responsibility: to create something that feels coherent, effortless and ultimately human.”
The owner can also choose the shipyard responsible for bringing the concept to life. That’s why the design firm explains the project was “conceived to explore the next generation of bespoke design.”
From the renderings revealed so far, Project White Arrow shapes up as an imposing superyacht with a sculptural profile. Its exterior is defined by long, uninterrupted lines, a plumb bow, and expansive glazing. An elongated foredeck and cascading aft decks create a sleek silhouette, while large stretches of glazing provide a close connection with the surrounding sea.
One of the project’s highlights is the aft deck, which is fitted with a glass-fronted swimming pool that extends above the beach club and swim platform, allowing outdoor relaxation and access to the water to intertwine. The expansive beach club leads to a wellness center with a sauna, steam room, two massage rooms and a full-beam gym with views across the water.
Project White Arrow is also envisioned with a winter garden with a working firepit, providing another space for gathering and relaxation, as well as a full-size pickleball court.
Photo: Nuvolari Lenard With a beam of almost 17 feet (5.2 meters), the superyacht offers 5,200 GT of interior volume. This means plenty of space for creating sprawling living quarters. And since the idea was to create a “home on the water,” the interior layout is designed to support extended stays, with nine staterooms and dedicated areas for privacy and common living.
The owner will benefit from an entire deck, complete with a private lounge, and there will also be accommodation for 40 crew members.
Other luxurious modern features that will be present onboard include a helipad, garage space for four tenders, and water toys for recreational activities beyond the yacht itself.
In terms of power, the yacht is set to feature a hybrid diesel-electric propulsion system, though no further details have been revealed yet.
All in all, Project White Arrow represents Nuvolari Lenard’s interpretation of a broader shift in how modern owners approach life at sea, with comfort, privacy, wellness and flexibility playing increasingly more important roles. But ultimately, the client will have the opportunity to put their own stamp on the yacht’s design and onboard experience.
“The most interesting projects are not necessarily those that arrive with every answer already defined,” concludes Dan Lenard. “They are the ones that establish a strong vision and leave the right space for the owner to make it their own.”
